scenes.voiceover: High above the city of Athens stands the Parthenon, a temple of white marble built to honour the goddess Athena. For more than two thousand years, it has watched over the people below.
scenes.visual: Stick figure citizens in tunics walking up the stone steps toward the Parthenon on the Acropolis hill at golden hour, the city of Athens spread out below.

scenes.voiceover: Down in the busy marketplace, a barefoot old man named Socrates spent his days asking questions. He carried no books and wrote nothing down, yet his questions would change the way the world thinks.
scenes.visual: The ancient Athenian agora marketplace in warm afternoon light, stone colonnades, market stalls with amphorae and baskets of olives, a clear open square in the middle.

scenes.voiceover: In 490 BC, a messenger ran from the battlefield at Marathon all the way to Athens with news of victory. His legendary run is why we still race marathons today.
scenes.visual: An exhausted stick figure messenger running along a dusty road between olive trees, sweat flying, a dropped shield and helmet by the roadside.
